target_clause: A server generating a 401 (Unauthorized) response MUST send a WWW-Authenticate header field containing at least one challenge.
next_clause: A server MAY generate a WWW-Authenticate header field in other response messages to indicate that supplying credentials (or different credentials) might affect the response.

previous_clause: HTTP clients are expected to use QUIC PING frames to keep connections open while there are responses outstanding for requests or server pushes.
target_clause: If the client is not expecting a response from the server, allowing an idle connection to time out is preferred over expending effort maintaining a connection that might not be needed. A gateway MAY use PING to maintain connections in anticipation of need rather than incur the latency cost of connection establishment to servers.
next_clause: Servers SHOULD NOT use PING frames to keep a connection open.

previous_clause: Upon timeout, the sender MUST retransmit all unacknowledged CRYPTO data if possible.
target_clause: The sender MUST NOT declare in-flight crypto packets as lost when the crypto timer expires.
next_clause: On each consecutive expiration of the crypto timer without receiving an acknowledgement for a new packet, the sender MUST double the crypto retransmission timeout and set a timer for this period.

previous_clause: An endpoint is not expected to protect information about whether a packet was successfully decrypted, or the number of valid Stateless Reset Tokens.
target_clause: If the last 16 bytes of the datagram are identical in value to a Stateless Reset Token, the endpoint MUST enter the draining period and not send any further packets on this connection.

previous_clause: All other behaviors described as applying to the SVCB RR also apply to all SVCB-compatible RR types unless explicitly stated otherwise.
target_clause: When following an AliasMode record ([alias-mode]) of RR type $T , the followup query to the TargetName MUST also be for type $T.
next_clause: This document defines one SVCB-compatible RR type (other than SVCB itself): the HTTPS RR type ([https]), which avoids Attrleaf label prefixes [Attrleaf] in order to improve compatibility with wildcards and CNAMEs, which are widely used with HTTP.

previous_clause: When there is no data to send, the sender SHOULD send a PING or other ack-eliciting frame in a single packet, re-arming the PTO timer.
target_clause: Alternatively, instead of sending an ack-eliciting packet, the sender MAY mark any packets still in flight as lost.
next_clause: Doing so avoids sending an additional packet, but increases the risk that loss is declared too aggressively, resulting in an unnecessary rate reduction by the congestion controller.

previous_clause: If the client has sent requests on streams with a Stream ID greater than or equal to that indicated in the GOAWAY frame, those requests are considered rejected ([request-cancellation]). Clients SHOULD cancel any requests on streams above this ID.
target_clause: Servers MAY also reject requests on streams below the indicated ID if these requests were not processed.
next_clause: Requests on Stream IDs less than the Stream ID in the GOAWAY frame might have been processed; their status cannot be known until they are completed successfully, reset individually, or the connection terminates.

previous_clause: Implementations might choose to increase limits as streams are closed, to keep the number of streams available to peers roughly consistent.
target_clause: An endpoint that is unable to open a new stream due to the peer's limits SHOULD send a STREAMS_BLOCKED frame ([frame-streams-blocked]).
next_clause: This signal is considered useful for debugging.

previous_clause: MAX_STREAM_ID frames which do not increase the maximum stream ID MUST be ignored.
target_clause: A peer MUST NOT initiate a stream with a higher stream ID than the greatest maximum stream ID it has received.
next_clause: An endpoint MUST terminate a connection with a STREAM_ID_ERROR error if a peer initiates a stream with a higher stream ID than it has sent, unless this is a result of a change in the initial limits (see [zerortt-parameters]).

previous_clause: Pushed responses that are not cacheable MUST NOT be stored by any HTTP cache.
target_clause: They MAY be made available to the application separately.
next_clause: The server MUST include a value in the :authority pseudo-header field for which the server is authoritative (see [authority]).

previous_clause: However, a server might want to send only a subset of the data requested for reasons of its own, such as temporary unavailability, cache efficiency, load balancing, etc. Since a 206 response is self-descriptive, the client can still understand a response that only partially satisfies its range request.
target_clause: A client MUST inspect a 206 response's Content-Type and Content-Range field(s) to determine what parts are enclosed and whether additional requests are needed.
next_clause: A server that generates a 206 response MUST generate the following header fields, in addition to those required in the subsections below, if the field would have been sent in a 200 (OK) response to the same request: Date, Cache-Control, ETag, Expires, Content-Location, and Vary.

previous_clause: A token-based scheme allows the server to offload any state associated with validation to the client.
target_clause: For this design to work, the token MUST be covered by integrity protection against modification or falsification by clients.
next_clause: Without integrity protection, malicious clients could generate or guess values for tokens that would be accepted by the server.

previous_clause: The capacity available on the new path might not be the same as the old path.
target_clause: Packets sent on the old path SHOULD NOT contribute to congestion control or RTT estimation for the new path.
next_clause: On confirming a peer’s ownership of its new address, an endpoint MUST immediately reset the congestion controller and round-trip time estimator for the new path to initial values (see Sections A.3 and B.3 in [QUIC-RECOVERY]) unless it has knowledge that a previous send rate or round-trip time estimate is valid for the new path.

previous_clause: The sender of a stream sends just three frame types that affect the state of a stream at either sender or receiver: STREAM ([frame-stream]), STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED ([frame-stream-data-blocked]), and RESET_STREAM ([frame-reset-stream]).
target_clause: A sender MUST NOT send any of these frames from a terminal state (“Data Recvd” or “Reset Recvd”).
next_clause: A sender MUST NOT send STREAM or STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED after sending a RESET_STREAM; that is, in the terminal states and in the “Reset Sent” state.

previous_clause: A server MUST NOT use 0-RTT keys to protect packets; it uses 1-RTT keys to protect acknowledgements of 0-RTT packets.
target_clause: Clients MUST NOT attempt to decrypt 0-RTT packets it receives and instead MUST discard them.
next_clause: Note:: 0-RTT data can be acknowledged by the server as it receives it, but any packets containing acknowledgments of 0-RTT data cannot have packet protection removed by the client until the TLS handshake is complete.

previous_clause: Clients SHOULD NOT wait indefinitely for SETTINGS to arrive before sending requests, but SHOULD process received datagrams in order to increase the likelihood of processing SETTINGS before sending the first request.
target_clause: When a 0-RTT QUIC connection is being used, the initial value of each server setting is the value used in the previous session. Clients SHOULD store the settings the server provided in the HTTP/3 connection where resumption information was provided, but MAY opt not to store settings in certain cases (e.g., if the session ticket is received before the SETTINGS frame).
next_clause: A client MUST comply with stored settings -- or default values, if no values are stored -- when attempting 0-RTT.

previous_clause: Including connection ID values in transport parameters and verifying them ensures that that an attacker cannot influence the choice of connection ID for a successful connection by injecting packets carrying attacker-chosen connection IDs during the handshake.
target_clause: An endpoint MUST treat any of the following as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION:
next_clause: absence of the initial_source_connection_id transport parameter from either endpoint,

previous_clause: If an endpoint receives a second SETTINGS frame on the control stream, the endpoint MUST respond with a connection error of type H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED.
target_clause: SETTINGS frames MUST NOT be sent on any stream other than the control stream.
next_clause: If an endpoint receives a SETTINGS frame on a different stream, the endpoint MUST respond with a connection error of type H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED.

previous_clause: Continue connection establishment as in [client-behavior] if necessary.
target_clause: As a latency optimization, clients MAY prefetch DNS records for later steps before they are needed.

previous_clause: When the PTO is armed for Initial or Handshake packet number spaces, the max_ack_delay in the PTO period computation is set to 0, since the peer is expected to not delay these packets intentionally; see 13.2.1 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT].
target_clause: The PTO period MUST be at least kGranularity, to avoid the timer expiring immediately.
next_clause: When ack-eliciting packets in multiple packet number spaces are in flight, the timer MUST be set to the earlier value of the Initial and Handshake packet number spaces.

previous_clause: If the Destination Connection ID is zero length and the packet matches the address/port tuple of a connection where the host did not require connection IDs, QUIC processes the packet as part of that connection. Endpoints MUST drop packets with zero-length Destination Connection ID fields if they do not correspond to a single connection.
target_clause: Endpoints SHOULD send a Stateless Reset ([stateless-reset]) for any packets that cannot be attributed to an existing connection.
next_clause: Packets that are matched to an existing connection, but for which the endpoint cannot remove packet protection, are discarded.

previous_clause: To reduce the chances of misinterpreting congestive loss as packets dropped by a faulty network element, an endpoint could set the ECT(0) codepoint in the first ten outgoing packets on a path, or for a period of three RTTs, whichever occurs first.
target_clause: Implementations MAY experiment with and use other strategies for use of ECN.
next_clause: Other methods of probing paths for ECN support are possible, as are different marking strategies.

previous_clause: QUIC hosts MUST NOT send packets if they would increase bytes_in_flight (defined in [vars-of-interest]) beyond the available congestion window, unless the packet is a probe packet sent after a PTO timer expires, as described in [pto].
target_clause: Implementations MAY use other congestion control algorithms, such as Cubic [RFC8312], and endpoints MAY use different algorithms from one another.
next_clause: The signals QUIC provides for congestion control are generic and are designed to support different algorithms.

previous_clause: The MAX_STREAM_DATA frame (type=0x11) is used in flow control to inform a peer of the maximum amount of data that can be sent on a stream.
target_clause: An endpoint that receives a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for a receive-only stream MUST terminate the connection with error PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
next_clause: An endpoint that receives a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for a send-only stream it has not opened MUST terminate the connection with error PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

previous_clause: When this is true, a server MAY request that the client abort transmission of a request without error by sending a RST_STREAM with an error code of NO_ERROR after sending a complete response and closing its stream.
target_clause: Clients MUST NOT discard responses as a result of receiving such a RST_STREAM, though clients can always discard responses at their discretion for other reasons.

previous_clause: A server MUST NOT send a Content-Length header field in any response with a status code of 1xx (Informational) or 204 (No Content).
target_clause: A server MUST NOT send a Content-Length header field in any 2xx (Successful) response to a CONNECT request ([CONNECT]).
next_clause: Aside from the cases defined above, in the absence of Transfer-Encoding, an origin server SHOULD send a Content-Length header field when the content size is known prior to sending the complete header section.

previous_clause: The server MUST include all settings that differ from their default values.
target_clause: If a server accepts 0-RTT but then sends settings that are not compatible with the previously specified settings, this MUST be treated as a connection error of type H3_SETTINGS_ERROR.
next_clause: If a server accepts 0-RTT but then sends a SETTINGS frame that omits a setting value that the client understands (apart from reserved setting identifiers) that was previously specified to have a non-default value, this MUST be treated as a connection error of type H3_SETTINGS_ERROR.

previous_clause: An origin server MUST, upon receiving an HTTP/1.1 (or later) request that has a method, target URI, and complete header section that contains a 100-continue expectation and indicates a request payload will follow, either send an immediate response with a final status code, if that status can be determined by examining just the method, target URI, and header fields, or send an immediate 100 (Continue) response to encourage the client to send the request payload.
target_clause: The origin server MUST NOT wait for the payload before sending the 100 (Continue) response.
next_clause: A proxy MUST, upon receiving an HTTP/1.1 (or later) request that has a method, target URI, and complete header section that contains a 100-continue expectation and indicates a request payload will follow, either send an immediate response with a final status code, if that status can be determined by examining just the method, target URI, and header fields, or begin forwarding the request toward the origin server by sending a corresponding request-line and header section to

previous_clause: This limits the magnitude of any amplification attack that can be mounted using spoofed source addresses.
target_clause: For the purposes of avoiding amplification prior to address validation, servers MUST count all of the payload bytes received in datagrams that are uniquely attributed to a single connection.
next_clause: This includes datagrams that contain packets that are successfully processed and datagrams that contain packets that are all discarded.

previous_clause: A STREAM frame with a FIN bit set or RST_STREAM causes the final offset for a stream to be fixed.
target_clause: The maximum data offset on a stream MUST NOT exceed the stream flow control offset advertised by the receiver.
next_clause: The sum of the maximum data offsets of all streams (including closed streams) MUST NOT exceed the connection flow control offset advertised by the receiver.

previous_clause: A server can store the expiration time or include it in an encrypted form in the token.
target_clause: A token issued with NEW_TOKEN MUST NOT include information that would allow values to be linked by an observer to the connection on which it was issued, unless the values are encrypted.
next_clause: For example, it cannot include the previous connection ID or addressing information.

previous_clause: Keep-alive packets MUST only be sent when no data or acknowledgement packets have been received for the connection within an interval.
target_clause: This interval MUST be configurable and MUST default to no less than two hours.
next_clause: It is extremely important to remember that ACK segments that contain no data are not reliably transmitted by TCP.

previous_clause: - Changed the text to require that IPv6 nodes must not create overlapping fragments.
target_clause: Also, when reassembling an IPv6 datagram, if one or more its constituent fragments is determined to be an overlapping fragment, the entire datagram (and any constituent fragments, including those not yet received) MUST be silently discarded.
next_clause: Includes clarification that no ICMP error message should be sent if overlapping fragments are received.

previous_clause: The most appropriate error code ([error-codes]) SHOULD be included in the frame that signals the error.
target_clause: Where this specification identifies error conditions, it also identifies the error code that is used; though these are worded as requirements, different implementation strategies might lead to different errors being reported. In particular, an endpoint MAY use any applicable error code when it detects an error condition; a generic error code (such as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION or INTERNAL_ERROR) can always be used in place of specific error codes.
next_clause: A stateless reset ([stateless-reset]) is not suitable for any error that can be signaled with a CONNECTION_CLOSE or RESET_STREAM frame.

section_heading: ServiceMode RR compatibility and mandatory keys
previous_clause: Keys MAY appear in any order, but MUST NOT appear more than once.
target_clause: For self-consistency ([service-mode]), listed keys MUST also appear in the SvcParams.
next_clause: To enable simpler parsing, this SvcParamValue MUST NOT contain escape sequences.

previous_clause: These packets can be processed once keys are provided by TLS.
target_clause: An endpoint SHOULD continue to respond to packets that can be processed during this time.
next_clause: After processing inputs, TLS might produce handshake bytes, keys for new encryption levels, or both.

previous_clause: 0-RTT and 1-RTT data exist in the same packet number space to make loss recovery algorithms easier to implement between the two packet types.
target_clause: A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a packet number within the same packet number space in one connection (that is, under the same cryptographic keys).
next_clause: If the packet number for sending reaches 2^62 - 1, the sender MUST close the connection without sending a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame or any further packets; an endpoint MAY send a Stateless Reset ([stateless-reset]) in response to further packets that it receives.

target_clause: Recursive resolvers MUST be able to convey SVCB records with unrecognized SvcParamKeys or malformed SvcParamValues. Resolvers MAY treat the entire SvcParams portion of the record as opaque.
next_clause: No part of this specification requires recursive resolvers to alter their behavior based on its contents, even if the contents are invalid.

previous_clause: Stream ID 0 cannot be reprioritized.
target_clause: A Prioritized Request ID that identifies Stream 0 MUST be treated as a connection error of type HTTP_MALFORMED_FRAME.
next_clause: A PRIORITY frame that does not reference a request MUST be treated as a HTTP_MALFORMED_FRAME error, unless it references Stream ID 0.

previous_clause: When a 0-RTT QUIC connection is being used, the initial value of each server setting is the value used in the previous session. Clients SHOULD store the settings the server provided in the HTTP/3 connection where resumption information was provided, but MAY opt not to store settings in certain cases (e.g., if the session ticket is received before the SETTINGS frame).
target_clause: A client MUST comply with stored settings -- or default values, if no values are stored -- when attempting 0-RTT.
next_clause: Once a server has provided new settings, clients MUST comply with those values.

previous_clause: An endpoint SHOULD supply a new connection ID when the peer retires a connection ID.
target_clause: If an endpoint provided fewer connection IDs than the peer's active_connection_id_limit, it MAY supply a new connection ID when it receives a packet with a previously unused connection ID.
next_clause: An endpoint MAY limit the total number of connection IDs issued for each connection to avoid the risk of running out of connection IDs; see [reset-token].

previous_clause: This allows the server push to be associated with a client request.
target_clause: When the same Push ID is promised on multiple request streams, the decompressed request field sections MUST contain the same fields in the same order, and both the name and the value in each field MUST be identical.
next_clause: The Push ID is then included with the push stream that ultimately fulfills those promises; see [push-streams].

previous_clause: If this happens, the sender SHOULD NOT send new data, but SHOULD retransmit normally the old unacknowledged data between SND.UNA and SND.UNA+SND.WND.
target_clause: The sender MAY also retransmit old data beyond SND.UNA+SND.WND, but SHOULD NOT time out the connection if data beyond the right window edge is not acknowledged.
next_clause: If the window shrinks to zero, the TCP MUST probe it in the standard way (described below).

previous_clause: Servers MUST drop incoming packets under all other circumstances.
target_clause: They SHOULD send a Stateless Reset ([stateless-reset]) if a connection ID is present in the header.

previous_clause: A field value does not include leading or trailing whitespace.
target_clause: When a specific version of HTTP allows such whitespace to appear in a message, a field parsing implementation MUST exclude such whitespace prior to evaluating the field value.
next_clause: Field values are usually constrained to the range of US-ASCII characters [USASCII].

previous_clause: No flags are defined for the HEADERS frame.
target_clause: A HEADERS frame with any flags set MUST be treated as a connection error of type HTTP_MALFORMED_HEADERS.
QUIC payloads MUST contain at least one frame, and MAY contain multiple frames and multiple frame types.
next_clause: Frames MUST fit within a single QUIC packet and MUST NOT span a QUIC packet boundary.

previous_clause: If these fields are present, they MUST NOT be empty.
target_clause: If both fields are present, they MUST contain the same value.
next_clause: If the scheme does not have a mandatory authority component and none is provided in the request target, the request MUST NOT contain the ":authority" pseudo-header or "Host" header fields.

previous_clause: Content received in a HEAD request has no defined semantics, cannot alter the meaning or target of the request, and might lead some implementations to reject the request and close the connection because of its potential as a request smuggling attack (Section 11.2 of [Messaging]).
target_clause: The response to a HEAD request is cacheable; a cache MAY use it to satisfy subsequent HEAD requests unless otherwise indicated by the Cache-Control header field (Section 5.2 of [Caching]).
next_clause: A HEAD response might also affect previously cached responses to GET; see Section 4.3.5 of [Caching].

previous_clause: Once an endpoint has completed sending all stream data and a STREAM frame with a FIN flag, the stream state becomes "half-closed (local)".
target_clause: When an endpoint receives all stream data and a FIN flag the stream state becomes "half-closed (remote)". An endpoint MUST NOT consider the stream state to have changed until all data has been sent or received.
next_clause: A RST_STREAM frame on an "open" stream also causes the stream to become "half-closed".

previous_clause: If the packet can be decrypted and authenticated using the updated key and IV, then the keys the endpoint uses for packet protection are also updated. The next packet sent by the endpoint MUST then use the new keys.
target_clause: Once an endpoint has sent a packet encrypted with a given key phase, it MUST NOT send a packet encrypted with an older key phase.
next_clause: An endpoint does not always need to send packets when it detects that its peer has updated keys.

previous_clause: HTTP/2 does not use the Connection header field (Section 7.6.1 of [HTTP]) to indicate connection-specific header fields; in this protocol, connection-specific metadata is conveyed by other means.
target_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT generate an HTTP/2 message containing connection-specific header fields; any message containing connection-specific header fields MUST be treated as malformed.
next_clause: The only exception to this is the TE header field, which MAY be present in an HTTP/2 request; when it is, it MUST NOT contain any value other than "trailers".

previous_clause: This means that any of these extension points can be safely used by extensions without prior arrangement or negotiation.
target_clause: However, where a known frame type is required to be in a specific location, such as the SETTINGS frame as the first frame of the control stream (see [control-streams]), an unknown frame type does not satisfy that requirement and SHOULD be treated as an error.
next_clause: Extensions that could change the semantics of existing protocol components MUST be negotiated before being used.

previous_clause: Following of HTTPS AliasMode RRs and CNAME aliases is unchanged from SVCB.
target_clause: Clients always convert "http" URLs to "https" before performing an HTTPS RR query using the process described in [hsts], so domain owners MUST NOT publish HTTPS RRs with a prefix of "_http".
next_clause: Note that none of these forms alter the HTTPS origin or authority.

previous_clause: Field name: The requested field name.
target_clause: It MUST conform to the field-name syntax defined in Section 5.1, and SHOULD be restricted to just letters, digits, hyphen ('-') and underscore ('_') characters, with the first character being a letter.
next_clause: Status: "permanent" or "provisional".
